Triage: graded on first touch (out of band of the concentrated rounds) because the `domain:services` seat has blocked #8231 on this card and asked for its grading explicitly — `finding` → **`needs-user-decision`**, routed `domain:devx` (whichever route is chosen, the change lands in `packages/lint`'s two test files, possibly plus `examples/app-showcase`), type `Task`, plus **`pm:blocking`** (open downstream dependent: #8231, blocker line recorded in its PM ruling comment of 16:50Z). This comment is from the triage seat Routine (session `session_0171b5csWnVxEc1G8qtYPxx5`).

Why this is a maintainer call and not auto-adjudicated: three of the four routes reduce regression-pin strength or keep a permanently-warning build — that is gate/test-weakening territory, which sits on the human floor regardless of prism alignment, and the prisms do not all point one way.

**The question:** for the last 3 nameless `app-showcase` sections, which route — (1) synthetic fixtures + name the 3 · (2) dedicated always-nameless fixture container · (3) assert-the-count · (4) accept the 3-warning floor?

Four-prism block:
- **Platform long-term coherence:** the current coupling inverts an invariant — the rule's only regression pin *requires shipped metadata to stay broken*. Any route that removes that inversion improves coherence; route (2) preserves the "fires on real shipped metadata" property but only by minting a must-never-be-fixed artifact, a new standing special case.
- **Measured business pull:** measured, not speculative — `translation-section-name-missing` has fired on every build since #5417 and was ignored long enough to accumulate 24 instances; PR #8514 took it to 3. A build that always warns trains everyone (and every agent) to ignore the warning; pull is toward zero.
- **AI-agent error-resistance:** a clean-loud build is the structurally safer temperature; a permanent warning floor is how this family went unacted-on. Route (2)'s fixture is exactly the thing a future sweep "fixes" despite the marker (the card itself concedes this); route (3) goes vacuous at count zero.
- **Startup scope discipline:** route (1) is the cheapest durable state — no permanent fixture obligation, no standing floor; the property lost ("pins on shipped metadata") can be approximated by deriving the synthetic fixture from a frozen snapshot of the pre-fix shipped shape.

**Recommendation: route (1)** — synthetic fixtures derived from a snapshot of the current shipped shape, then name the 3 sections; single cross-domain PR (`packages/lint` + `examples/app-showcase`) as #8231's ruling comment already sketches. Honest cost: the rule loses its live real-metadata pin; the snapshot-derived fixture keeps the shape realistic but no longer proves the rule fires on metadata that actually ships.

Decision here unblocks #8231 (its remainder then follows mechanically, one dispatch). Re-check lines: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/example-showcase build` (expect exactly 3 `translation-section-name-missing`); `git grep -n "reports both nameless headings" origin/main -- packages/lint`.

**Maintainer ruling recorded — synthetic fixtures, snapshot-derived; then name the three sections.** Provenance: maintainer live session, 2026-08-13 ~23:50Z, verbatim 「接受你的全部建议」, accepting this seat's four-prism briefing of the full decision box (this card's briefed recommendation: route 1 — synthetic fixtures derived from a snapshot of the currently-shipped metadata shape, then name the 3 remaining sections).

**The ruling, spelled out for dispatch:**
1. Move the three pinned lint tests (`validate-translatable-sections.test.ts` ×2, `validate-translation-references.test.ts` ×1) onto **synthetic fixtures derived from a snapshot of the shipped `app-showcase` shape** — realistic structure preserved, but no longer imported live from `examples/**`, so the fixtures cannot be "fixed" out from under the rule by an example-app sweep.
2. Then name the three sections (`showcase_task` edit "Task" · `showcase_task` quick "Quick Edit" · `showcase_contact` create "Who is this?") — this is #8231's remainder and clears the permanent 3-warning floor.
3. Explicitly rejected by the ruling: the dedicated always-nameless fixture app (a trap a future sweep will eventually "fix"), the count-only assertion (goes vacuous at zero), and accepting the warning floor (trains everyone to ignore the warning — the measured cause of this family going unacted-on).

Label transition: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`. `pm:blocking` retained — #8231 stays `Blocked-by` this card until the fixture migration lands; its remainder (step 2's naming, `examples/**`) can ride in the same PR or in #8231's own lane immediately after — implementing seat declares which.

Recorded by the triage seat on the maintainer's direct channel.
